items.title: PSMA-PET Guided Radiation for Recurrent Prostate Cancer After Surgery
items.summary: This completed trial used advanced PET imaging with PSMA tracer to locate cancer that returned after surgery and radiation. Researchers treated all identified cancer sites with precisely targeted radiation (SABR). This approach aims to find and destroy cancer deposits that standard scans miss when PSA rises after treatment.

items.title: Talazoparib for Advanced Cancers with DNA Repair Gene Mutations
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether the PARP inhibitor talazoparib works in patients with advanced cancer who have mutations in DNA repair genes. The study includes patients who have or haven't been treated with other PARP inhibitors. It may help determine if switching between different PARP inhibitors could benefit some patients.

items.title: 177Lu-PSMA-VG01 Phase 1 Trial for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1 trial evaluates a radioligand therapy called 177Lu-PSMA-VG01 in men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study examines safety, how the drug distributes in the body, radiation dosing, and early signs of anti-tumor activity. This is similar to FDA-approved Pluvicto but testing a different formulation.

items.title: Tulmimetostat Plus Enzalutamide for Advanced Solid Tumors and Lymphomas
items.summary: This first-in-human trial tests DZR123 (tulmimetostat), a drug targeting epigenetic enzymes, both alone and combined with enzalutamide in advanced cancers. The study evaluates safety, drug levels in the body, and early anti-tumor activity. This represents a novel mechanism that may help overcome resistance to hormone therapy.

items.title: TIL Cell Therapy for Metastatic Colorectal and Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1/2 trial tests a personalized cell therapy using tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (TIL) in patients with metastatic colorectal and prostate cancer. TIL therapy involves extracting immune cells from tumors, expanding them in the lab, and reinfusing them to fight cancer. This represents an immunotherapy approach for cancers typically resistant to checkpoint inhibitors.

items.title: Nivolumab, Ipilimumab, and Cabozantinib for Rare Genitourinary Tumors
items.summary: This phase 2 trial combines two immunotherapy drugs (nivolumab and ipilimumab) with cabozantinib, a targeted drug that blocks tumor blood vessel growth. The study treats patients with rare genitourinary cancers that have spread and have no other treatment options. The combination may work better than any single drug alone.

items.title: AI Prediction of Prostate Cancer Metastasis from Biopsy
items.summary: This observational study develops artificial intelligence to analyze prostate cancer biopsy specimens and predict which patients are likely to have lymph node or distant metastasis. The AI model aims to provide additional information to help doctors make treatment and surgical decisions. This could help identify high-risk patients earlier.

items.title: Radium-223 Plus M3814 and Avelumab for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial tests combinations of radium-223 (bone-targeted radiation) with M3814 (a drug that blocks DNA repair) and avelumab (immunotherapy) in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer that has spread to bones. The study aims to find the best dose and determine which combination works better than radium-223 alone.

items.title: Lutetium-PSMA Plus Enzalutamide Versus Enzalutamide Alone for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 randomized trial compares enzalutamide alone to the combination of Lu-PSMA radioligand therapy plus enzalutamide in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy. The study evaluates whether adding PSMA-targeted radiation improves outcomes. Results could change treatment sequencing decisions.

items.title: Darolutamide Plus ADT After Surgery for High-Risk Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares adding darolutamide to standard androgen deprivation therapy versus ADT alone after prostate surgery in men with high-risk disease. Darolutamide is a newer hormone therapy that blocks testosterone effects. The study tests whether this combination better prevents cancer from returning after surgery.

items.title: Cognitive Effects of Darolutamide Versus Enzalutamide in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial compared cognitive side effects between darolutamide and enzalutamide in men with castration-resistant or hormone-sensitive metastatic prostate cancer. Using standardized cognitive testing, researchers assessed whether one drug causes less mental fog and memory problems. This addresses an important quality of life concern for patients.

items.title: Abiraterone With or Without Cabazitaxel After Docetaxel for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests whether adding cabazitaxel chemotherapy to abiraterone hormone therapy works better than abiraterone alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel. The study evaluates if combining these drugs helps kill more cancer cells and improves survival.

items.title: Testosterone Plus ZEN-3694 Followed by Enzalutamide Plus ZEN-3694
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests a novel strategy: first giving testosterone with ZEN-3694 (which blocks a protein called BRD4), then switching to enzalutamide with ZEN-3694 in castration-resistant prostate cancer. This approach targets the MYC cancer gene and tests whether temporarily increasing testosterone might make subsequent treatments work better.

items.title: Apalutamide, Abiraterone, and PSMA-PET Guided Radiation After Surgery
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests two questions in men whose PSA rises after prostate surgery. First, does adding apalutamide and abiraterone to standard prostate radiation and short-term hormone therapy improve outcomes? Second, for men with visible metastases on PET scan, does adding radiation to those spots help? This major trial could change post-surgery treatment standards.

items.title: Xaluritamig Plus Abiraterone Versus Standard Treatment for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial compares xaluritamig (an investigational bispecific antibody) plus abiraterone to investigator's choice treatment (docetaxel, cabazitaxel, or abiraterone) in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who haven't received chemotherapy. The primary goal is to determine if the combination improves overall survival.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Abiraterone First-Line for mCRPC China Study
items.summary: This phase 3 trial evaluates the combination of olaparib (a PARP inhibitor) and abiraterone versus abiraterone alone as first-line treatment for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in Chinese patients. The study tests whether adding a drug that blocks DNA repair improves outcomes when combined with hormone therapy.

items.title: GSK5458514 Alone or Combined for Prostate Cancer Treatment
items.summary: This phase 1/2 trial evaluates GSK5458514, an investigational drug, given alone or combined with other anti-cancer treatments in men with prostate cancer. The study will determine safe doses and assess how well the body handles the drug while looking for early signs of effectiveness.

items.title: 177Lu-TLX591 Plus Standard Care Versus Standard Care for mCRPC
items.summary: This phase 3 trial tests whether adding 177Lu-TLX591 (a PSMA-targeted radioligand therapy) to standard treatment improves outcomes compared to standard treatment alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer who progressed after hormone therapy. This is similar to FDA-approved Pluvicto but tests a different formulation.

items.title: First-in-Human Study of GSK5471713 for mCRPC
items.summary: This first-in-human phase 1/2 trial evaluates the safety, tolerability, drug levels, and early clinical activity of GSK5471713 given alone in men with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The study will establish safe dosing and determine the drug's benefit-risk profile for future development.

items.title: Abemaciclib With or Without Atezolizumab for Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This completed phase 2 trial tested whether abemaciclib (a targeted chemotherapy blocking cell cycle proteins) and atezolizumab (immunotherapy), alone or combined, are effective in shrinking or preventing growth of metastatic prostate cancer. The study also evaluated safety of the combination. Results could inform future treatment strategies.

items.title: Low Dose Naltrexone for Fatigue in Men on Hormone Therapy
items.summary: This upcoming phase 2 trial will test whether low-dose naltrexone (3mg daily) can reduce fatigue in men with prostate cancer receiving androgen deprivation therapy or newer hormone medicines. Fatigue is a common and debilitating side effect of hormone therapy, and this trial could offer a simple treatment option.

items.title: PSMA-Targeted Therapy for Low-Volume Metastatic Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This phase 2 trial tests adding 177Lu-PSMA-617 radioligand therapy to standard hormone treatment, with or without abiraterone, in men with newly diagnosed or recurrent low-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer. The study evaluates whether adding PSMA-targeted radiation earlier in treatment improves outcomes when disease is still limited.

items.title: Inflammation Drives Castration-Resistant Prostate Cancer Development
items.summary: This research review explains how chronic inflammation reprograms prostate cancer cells to become resistant to hormone therapy. Inflammatory pathways like NFκB and IL6/JAK/STAT3 work together with androgen receptor signaling to promote tumor survival, growth, spread, and immune evasion. These pathways also change the cancer's genetic and epigenetic landscape, suggesting new treatment targets.

items.title: PSMA DNA Vaccine Enhances Immunotherapy Response in Prostate Cancer
items.summary: This preclinical study developed a novel DNA vaccine targeting PSMA using nanoplasmid technology. The vaccine generated strong immune responses against prostate cancer and prevented lung metastasis in animal models. When combined with PD-1 checkpoint blockade, it enhanced anti-tumor immunity. This represents a potential new immunotherapy approach for metastatic castration-resistant disease.

items.title: Olaparib Plus Radium-223 Phase 2 Trial Results
items.source: Journal of clinical oncology : official journal of the American Society of Clinical Oncology
items.summary: This multicenter phase 2 trial compared the PARP inhibitor olaparib combined with radium-223 bone-targeted radiation versus radium-223 alone in men with castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases. The study evaluated whether combining drugs that block DNA repair with radiation to bones improves outcomes. Results could inform treatment strategies for bone-metastatic disease.

items.title: Rucaparib Drug Review for BRCA-Mutated Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This drug evaluation reviews rucaparib, a PARP inhibitor approved for treating metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer in men with BRCA1/2 or other DNA repair gene mutations. The review discusses how rucaparib works, its clinical efficacy, side effects, and role in treating patients with specific genetic mutations.

items.title: Dual BRD4/AKT Inhibitor Overcomes c-MYC Resistance in mCRPC
items.summary: This research developed a novel drug that simultaneously blocks BRD4 and AKT proteins in metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. The dual inhibitor addresses a key resistance mechanism: when AKT inhibitors alone are used, c-MYC levels rise and drive resistance. By blocking both pathways, the compound (21d) showed strong anti-cancer activity in laboratory studies.

items.title: Patient Quality of Life with Radium-223 Plus Olaparib
items.summary: This study reports patient-reported outcomes from men with castration-resistant prostate cancer and bone metastases treated with radium-223 with or without olaparib. The analysis examines how the treatments affected quality of life, pain, fatigue, and other symptoms. Understanding patient experience helps inform treatment decisions beyond just survival data.

items.title: Machine Learning Predicts Survival in Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases
items.source: The aging male : the official journal of the International Society for the Study of the Aging Male
items.summary: This study developed a machine learning model to predict overall survival in men with prostate cancer and bone metastases who don't undergo surgery. Using data from over 3,000 patients, the model identified Gleason score as the most important survival predictor, more important than tumor stage. This tool could help doctors identify high-risk patients for aggressive early treatment.

items.title: New ALDH7A1 Inhibitors Show Promise for Prostate Cancer
items.source: Journal of enzyme inhibition and medicinal chemistry
items.summary: This research identified new drugs that target ALDH7A1, an enzyme that drives prostate cancer growth and progression. The inhibitors selectively block ALDH7A1 activity and showed anti-cancer effects in laboratory studies. ALDH7A1 is particularly important in castration-resistant disease, making it an attractive target for drug development.

items.title: Meta-Analysis of Immunotherapy Efficacy in Metastatic CRPC
items.summary: This comprehensive analysis of 21 clinical trials including 1,580 patients examined immunotherapy effectiveness in unselected metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer. Results showed modest benefits with 63% one-year survival and better outcomes when immunotherapy was combined with other treatments. The findings highlight that while immunotherapy shows promise, combination approaches may be most effective.
